blocks.text: At first we intended to use very little music: within the realistic aesthetic of the podcast, music heard only by the audience felt artificial. That changed once the podcast took shape as a movement between two worlds — Jaïr's interviews, edited down to his answers, and the scenes of the implicit listener. Moving between them could feel disorienting.

"The solution we found was to use brief musical compositions, to smooth these transitions — teleports of sorts, between current reality and the reality of the implicit listener. As my musical compositions took on a more substantial role in the podcast, we also discovered that they added a dramatic element that supported the narrative." — Amit
